scope: Local implementation of QR-2 sub-slice S4-2 (RC-Q38): the pure owner-total allocation module src/portfolio/qr2-allocation.js and its unit tests. It reads no database and is wired into no route, worker or view.
method: The S4 design as in RC-Q37. A coder (Sonnet 5.5) wrote S4-2; an independent architecture auditor (Opus 5.5) reviewed it for double counting and partial totals and found that an account of a Bot created after the range failed the request; root ruled on that and five smaller findings; the coder fixed them; an independent tester (Sonnet 5.5) ran single-edit mutations after each round. A sole-runner tester then ran, with nothing else active, every test file that imports a changed module of this batch (found with git grep): 22 PostgreSQL files one file per process on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster (392 tests, 0 fail; 2 skipped by the TEMP-privilege environment gate in a file this batch did not change), the full unit suite (2214 tests, 0 fail, 6 skipped by platform gates, 9 todo) and the grant text test; every changed file had the same hash before and after. Nobody verified their own work.
hashNote: SHA-256 of the line-feed content as Git stores it.
result: test/qr2-allocation.test.js 34 of 34 pass, with hand-computed fixtures; the QR-2 response and portfolio tests pass unchanged.
limits: Provisional until the owner decides the S4 items: the strict reading that a range starting before a declaration takes effect has no total.
Whether the summed fees are cumulative or range fees (8.1) stays open.
The S4-5 adapter must supply NAV at both ends, price states and the RX keys per account; the composed per-Bot response does not carry all of them today.
Not wired; no owner total is computed anywhere.

rootAcceptance.statement: Root reviewed the agent reports, the rulings, the sole-runner verification and the final diff and accepted S4-2 as local engineering evidence for the QR-2 row. Acceptance changes no PM-1 credit by itself and deploys nothing.
